title: Penguins Keep Their Feet at 0°C On Purpose 🐧
description:
How do penguins keep their feet from freezing on the ice? Warm blood flowing down their legs runs right beside cold blood coming back up, so heat is swapped before it reaches the feet (countercurrent heat exchange), and the feet stay just above freezing while rocking back on their heels and tail keeps the toes off the ice.

Sources:
https://www.britannica.com/animal/penguin/Form-and-function
https://www.howitworksdaily.com/why-dont-penguins-feet-freeze/
https://interestingengineering.com/science/why-dont-penguins-feet-freeze-evolutionary-adaptation

Animated in the Low-Poly Faceted style.

topic: How do penguins keep their feet from freezing?
script:
You'd lose your toes on this ice.
Emperor penguins stand on it for two months.
The secret is in their legs.
Warm blood flowing down to the feet
runs right beside cold blood coming back up.
So the heat jumps across,
like passing a hot potato.
By the time blood reaches the toes,
it's just above freezing.
Cold toes lose very little heat to the ice,
and the warmth goes back into the body.
Feet near zero degrees,
body near thirty-eight.
If the toes get too cold,
the penguin widens its arteries,
and sends down a little more warm blood.
Still chilly?
It rocks back on its heels and stiff tail,
lifting its toes off the ice,
and hunches down,
so belly feathers blanket its feet.
A penguin keeps its feet cold on purpose.
So how long would your toes last out there?
key_facts: Penguin legs use countercurrent heat exchange: arteries and veins run closely side by side so outgoing warm blood warms the cold blood returning from the feet (Britannica, How It Works)
Penguins keep their feet just above freezing; Britannica puts foot skin temperature near 0 °C
Penguins can increase warm blood flow to the feet by widening the arteries if the feet get too cold (How It Works)
Penguins rock back on their heels and tail to lift their feet off the ice, and hunch so belly feathers cover the feet (How It Works)
Male emperor penguins stand on the sea ice incubating the egg for about two months; penguin core body temperature is about 38 °C
